questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.**

Pratham will not go to the party __if__ he is personally invited.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**unless.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The preposition 'if' must be replaced with the conjunction of condition 'unless'.
 
• **Unless: **except if (used to introduce the case in which a statement being made is not true or valid)
 
• It determines the condition why Pratham will not go to the party.
 
• The conjunction of reason 'because' is wrong. *Pratham will not go to the party because__ he is personally invited.*
 
• Adverb 'even' makes the sentence grammatically incorrect.

**The correct sentence**: __*Pratham will not go to the party **unless** he is personally invited.*__

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and make a grammatically correct sentence.

Your need is certainly greater than ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2.**

**Mine **is a possessive pronoun. 

 
• In the sentence, "Your need is certainly greater than mine," the word "mine" is a possessive pronoun that is used to refer back to the speaker. It is used to indicate that the speaker is making a comparison between the other person's need and their own need.
 
• Here, "mine" is used in place of "my need", where "my" is the possessive adjective that indicates possession of the noun "need". In this case, the possessive pronoun "mine" is used to indicate that the speaker's need is less important or less urgent than the need of the other person.
 
• Therefore, the correct option to fill in the blank is "mine", which indicates that the speaker is making a comparison between the other person's need and their own need. The sentence thus means that the other person's need is greater than the speaker's need.

The personal pronoun **I** is wrong. The sentence becomes grammatically incorrect.

Also, pronouns **Me** and **My** are grammatically incorrect.

Thus the correct sentence will be: Your need is certainly greater than mine.

One of the friends were doubtful that the plan would work.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1.**

The sentence is specific about 'one' of the friends, so it is clear that it is one individual and not many.

The verb must agree with its subject in number and person. Thus, if the subject is of the singular number, the verb must also be of the singular number.

Thus **were** would change to **was.**

Thus the correct sentence will be: *One of the friends was doubtful that the plan would work.*

questions.question:

Timely alerts about floods in Bhutan ______ a blessing to Indian villages.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1.**

The Subject-Verb agreement rule says The verb must agree with its subject in Number and Person.

Thus, the subject of the sentence is in the plural form and hence the verb will also be in plural form.

The sentence is in the Present tense, and the usage of 'have' is correct.

The other options with verbs in the present tense singular and plural form makes the sentence grammatically incorrect.

The error is in the phrase 'as a salary offered' with the use of indefinite article **A.**

A definite article must be used, as it refers to Nisha's salary. It is particularly hers.

questions.question: If RACK = 9; TOP = 5; then, MAPLE = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e364f39ec5ab4e4a033d423e608bf1e8a1eb03483a0ad0fe11fd6c8faf32c44.png] 

The pattern followed is,

For RACK,

R → 18, A → 1, C → 3, K → 11

18 + 1 + 3 + 11 = 33

3 × 3 = 9

RACK → 9

For TOP,

T → 20, O → 15, P → 16

20 + 15 + 16 = 51

5 × 1 = 5

TOP → 5

Similarly,

For MAPLE,

M → 13, A → 1, P → 16, L → 12, E → 5

13 + 1 + 16 + 12 + 5 = 47

4 × 7 = 28

MAPLE → **28**

Hence, “28” is the correct answer.

questions.question: Pankaj invests an amount by dividing it between three different schemes A, B and C with rates of interest, 10%, 12% and 15% per annum respectively, and the total interest that accumulates in one year is Rs. 3200. The amount he invests in schemes A, B and C are in the proportion 8 : 5 : 12, then what is the amount he invests in scheme B?
questions.solution:
The interest rates are 10%, 12% and 15% per annum.

Time = 1 year

The ratio of invested amount = 8x : 5x : 12x

As we know,

SI = Prt/100

According to the question

(8x × 10 × 1)/100 + (5x × 12 × 1)/100 + (12x × 15 × 1)/100 = 3200

⇒ (80x/100) + (60x/100) + (180x/100) = 3200

⇒ (80x + 60x + 180x)/100 = 3200

⇒ 320x/100 = 3200

⇒ x = 3200 × (100/320)

⇒ x = 1000

∴ Money invested in B = 5 × 1000 = Rs. 5000

**Short trick:**

The interest rates are 10%, 12% and 15% per annum.

A = 80 and B = 50 and C = 120

⇒ (8 + 6 + 18) unit = 3200

⇒ 32 unit = 3200

⇒ 1 unit = 100

⇒ 50 unit = 100 × 50 = 5000

∴ Money invested in B = 5 × 1000 = Rs. 500

questions.question: An inlet pipe can fill an empty tank in 2 hours and an outlet pipe can empty the full tank in 3 hours. In what time will the empty tank get filled, if the inlet and the outlet pipes are opened together?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

An inlet pipe can fill an empty tank in 2 hours and an outlet pipe can empty the full tank in 3 hours. 

Formula used:

For LCM method,

If a pipe fills a tank in 'a' hours and an another empties the same tank in 'b' hours and they are opened together, then

Total work = LCM of the times taken by two pipes = LCM of (a, b)

Efficiency of first pipe = LCM of (a, b)/a

Efficiency of second pipe = LCM of (a, b)/b

Combined efficiency of them = (+ efficiency of 1st pipe) + (- efficiency of 2nd pipe)

[(+ve) sign for the efficiency of the pipe which fills the tank and (-ve) sign for the efficiency of the pipe which empties the tank.]

Time taken to fill the tank = Total work/The combined efficiency of the pipes.

For Alternate method,

If a pipe fills a tank in 'a' hours and an another empties the same tank in 'b' hours and they are opened together, the net part filled in 1 hour = 1/a - 1/b

∴ Time taken to fill the tank = 1/(1/a - 1/b) = ab/(b - a) hours

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/afe3a7cac67016cac84cbc6210b8342eef010913fa029eb008940cd2a0e492a4.png] 

In fig, LCM of (2, 3) = Total work = 6

Efficiency of Inlet pipe = + 6/2 = + 3

Efficiency of Outlet pipe = - 6/3 = - 2

Combined efficiency = 3 - 2 = 1

If both pipes open together, then the tank filled in = 6/1 = 6 hours

**∴ Time taken to fill the tank is 6 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4dc8c3e83508eaf43bce3e473329500aa0b5140181df4d5d2a28e24bd3c31c58.png] 

Inlet pipe fills in 2 hours

Outlet pipe empties in 3 hours

So time taken to fill the tank = (2 × 3)/(3 - 2) = 6 hours

**∴ Time taken to fill the tank is 6 hours.**
